narrative:
The model determined that you have a 51% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over 50%, the bank decided to deny your loan application.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account status was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only 12.6% of them show this status—whereas most approved borrowers have either no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

The requested loan duration of 12 months worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval. Approved applicants typically ask for almost 20 months on average, so your shorter term was viewed positively. The purpose of the loan (domestic appliances) also slightly reduced the risk score, though its effect was smaller.

Overall, the negative signal from your checking account outweighed the positive contributions from the shorter duration and loan purpose, tipping the model past the approval threshold.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account—aim to clear any overdraft and maintain a positive balance for several months—before reapplying. This single change is likely to have the biggest impact on future decisions. (218 words)
